prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: warehouse, receiving to outbound load release. Elements: Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (records vehicle/carrier/trailer/arrival; validates vs receiving plan; flags unscheduled; directs to door; uses Trailer Seal Exception Note; blocks risky vehicle); Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork/seals; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note; consumes inspection advisory, records proceed/rework/hold); Pallet Dimension Scanner, alias Moonquarry (produces Oversize Load Advisory, never authorizes rule-violating placement); Inbound Pallet Buffer (temporary staging, not inventory acceptance); North/South Aisle Stacker Crane (report availability; North alias Juniperwake sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot, uses Slot Reservation Receipt to confirm destination, checks task state before moving, stops if destination/path invalid, reports positioning/retention/braking/travel faults); East/West Transfer Conveyor; Conveyor Line Controller, alias Brasshaven (produces Transfer Induction Ticket; stops on unsafe downstream; holds transfers on uncertain exception); Autonomous Forklift Fleet, alias Larkspur (produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation); Outbound Dispatch Sorter (receives Dispatch Wave Amendment); Outbound Checkweigh Scale (produces Gross Weight Variance Slip when out of tolerance; unresolved until reweigh or documented safe disposition); Shipping Documentation Desk; Safety Zone Controller, Fire Alarm Panel (produces Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice; both retain authority to stop/restrict movement); Maintenance Release Terminal, alias Copperfield (produces Crane Service Release Card; records inspection outcome and authorizer). Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authoritative state; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; consumes load advisory to apply handling constraints; blocks incompatible allocation while advisory applies. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (reviews holds, escalates unresolved, checks delays vs outbound waves/aisle limits, releases normal work only after exceptions, maintenance holds, access constraints reconciled); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel; maintenance personnel. Requirements: no work without WMS release; unique task ref; damaged/held pallets separated until review validated; blocked task records hold reason and last confirmed location; attribute mismatch blocks auto-allocation; record scan result/location/time. Maintenance: fault recorded, controlled area, separated from live movement; crane unavailable during inspection; failed test keeps inhibited, back to queue; pass needs interlock/limit checks before release; authorization recorded. Cranes stay in aisle. Conveyors: interlocks, one-at-a-time

New part:
S172: A recovery response begins when a position discrepancy, obstruction, or safety alarm makes continued automatic movement uncertain.
S173: Fire Alarm Panel and Safety Zone Controller retain authority to stop or restrict movement whenever their safety status requires it.
S174: Safety Zone Controller establishes a controlled boundary around the affected aisle and prevents new equipment from entering it.
S175: Warehouse Operations Supervisor verifies that personnel are clear of the boundary before authorizing recovery work.
S176: Conveyor Line Controller holds transfers that could feed material into the isolated area.
S177: Morrowglass, the Warehouse Management System, receives the occupancy snapshot for recovery planning.
S178: Warehouse Management System reconciles its location records with available sensor data before it presents a recovery plan.
S179: Velvetrook applies the yard exception by holding affected vehicle movements outside the recovery boundary.
S180: Yard traffic remains under controlled access until the aisle is confirmed safe for normal operations.
S181: The recovery plan identifies the permitted travel envelope, the expected stopping point, and the conditions that require an immediate stop.
S182: South Aisle Stacker Crane performs a controlled recovery maneuver at reduced speed within the isolated aisle.
S183: The maneuver uses only the travel needed to reach a stable position or clear the obstruction under review.
S184: Personnel remain outside the crane travel envelope throughout the maneuver.
S185: A spotter may observe from a protected location but does not enter the isolated aisle while motion is enabled.
S186: Any unexpected movement, loss of position confidence, or renewed alarm causes an immediate stop and reassessment.
S187: Safety Zone Controller maintains the boundary until the cause of the stop has been understood and the recovery plan has been checked again.
S188: Inbound Pallet Buffer remains unavailable to new receipts when its access path intersects the isolated area.
S189: East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor remain stopped where their movement could compromise the boundary.
S190: Autonomous Forklift Fleet receives a hold instruction for routes that approach the recovery area.
S191: Maintenance Release Terminal records the inspection outcome and any repair work required before equipment can return to service.
S192: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reconciles outstanding exceptions, maintenance holds, and access constraints before releasing normal work.
S193: A controlled test confirms that the equipment responds correctly to stop commands and that its reported position is stable.
S194: The isolation boundary is removed only after the test passes and the aisle is clear of personnel and loose material.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
